43_1_1: In the beginning, the Word already was — face-to-face with God, and Himself God.
43_1_2: He was there, in the beginning, with God.
43_1_3: Through Him everything came to be. Without Him, not one thing that exists came into being.
43_1_4: In Him was life, and that life was the light of every person.
43_1_5: The light keeps shining into the darkness, and the darkness has never overcome it — nor understood it.
43_1_6: A man came, sent from God. His name was John.
43_1_7: He came as a witness — to testify about the Light, so that through him, everyone might come to believe.
43_1_8: He himself was not the Light; he was sent to bear witness to the Light.
43_1_9: The true Light — the Light that gives light to every person — was now coming into the world.
43_1_10: He was in the world, and the world came into being through Him, yet the world did not recognize Him.
43_1_11: He came to what was His own, and His own people did not receive Him.
43_1_12: But to all who received Him — all who believed on His name — He gave the right to become children of God,
43_1_13: born not from bloodlines, nor from human desire, nor from a husband's will, but born of God Himself.
43_1_14: And the Word became flesh. He pitched His tent among us, and we saw His glory with our own eyes — the glory of the Father's one-and-only Son, full of grace and full of truth.
43_1_15: John testified about Him and called out: "This is the One I was speaking of when I said, 'The One coming after me has outranked me, because He existed before me.'"
43_1_16: From His fullness we have all received — one grace piled on another, grace in exchange for grace.
43_1_17: The law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
43_1_18: No one has ever seen God. The one-and-only Son, Himself God, who rests at the Father's side — He is the One who has made Him known.
43_1_19: This is the testimony of John, when the Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
43_1_20: He confessed it openly; he did not deny, but confessed: "I am not the Christ."
43_1_21: So they asked him, "What then? Are you Elijah?" He said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" He answered, "No."
43_1_22: Then they said, "Who are you — so we can give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?"
43_1_23: He said, "I am the voice of one calling out in the wilderness: 'Make the way of the Lord straight,' just as the prophet Isaiah said."
43_1_24: Now those who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
43_1_25: They pressed him: "Why then are you baptizing — if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"
43_1_26: John answered them, "I baptize with water. But standing among you is One you do not know —
43_1_27: the One coming after me, whose sandal-strap I am not worthy to untie."
43_1_28: These things happened in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
43_1_29: The next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, "Look! — the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
43_1_30: This is the One I was speaking of when I said, 'A man is coming after me who has outranked me, because He existed before me.'
43_1_31: I myself did not know who He was — but the reason I came baptizing with water was so that He might be revealed to Israel."
43_1_32: Then John testified: "I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and He remained on Him.
43_1_33: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water said to me, 'The One on whom you see the Spirit descend and remain — He is the One who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'
43_1_34: And I have seen it. I testify: this is the Son of God."
43_1_35: The next day, John was standing there again with two of his disciples,
43_1_36: and as he watched Jesus walking by, he said, "Look — the Lamb of God!"
43_1_37: The two disciples heard him say it and followed Jesus.
43_1_38: Jesus turned and saw them following, and asked them, "What are you looking for?" They said to Him, "Rabbi" (which translates 'Teacher'), "where are You staying?"
43_1_39: He told them, "Come, and you will see." So they came and saw where He was staying, and they stayed with Him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
43_1_40: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was one of the two who had heard John and followed Jesus.
43_1_41: He first found his own brother Simon and told him, "We have found the Messiah" (which translates 'the Christ').
43_1_42: He brought him to Jesus. Looking at him, Jesus said, "You are Simon, son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas" (which translates 'Peter').
43_1_43: The next day, Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and told him, "Follow Me."
43_1_44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.
43_1_45: Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law — and the Prophets, too — Jesus of Nazareth, son of Joseph."
43_1_46: Nathanael said to him, "From Nazareth? Can anything good come out of there?" Philip said, "Come and see."
43_1_47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward Him and said about him, "Look — a true Israelite, a man in whom there is no deceit!"
43_1_48: Nathanael said to Him, "How do You know me?" Jesus answered, "Before Philip called you, when you were still under the fig tree, I saw you."
43_1_49: Nathanael answered, "Rabbi, You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"
43_1_50: Jesus answered him, "You believe because I said I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these."
43_1_51: And He said to him, "Truly, truly, I tell you — you will all see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man."
43_2_1: On the third day, there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
43_2_2: Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
43_2_3: When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to Him, "They have no wine."
43_2_4: Jesus said to her, "Woman, why does that involve Me? My hour has not yet come."
43_2_5: His mother told the servants, "Whatever He tells you to do, do it."
43_2_6: Now six stone water jars were standing there, used for the Jewish purification rites, each holding twenty or thirty gallons.
43_2_7: Jesus told the servants, "Fill the jars with water." And they filled them to the brim.
43_2_8: Then He said, "Now draw some out and take it to the head steward." So they took it.
43_2_9: When the head steward tasted the water — now become wine — and he did not know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew, he called the bridegroom
43_2_10: and said to him, "Everyone serves the good wine first, and then, after the guests have had plenty to drink, the lesser wine. But you have saved the best wine until now!"
43_2_11: This — the first of His signs — Jesus performed in Cana of Galilee. He revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
43_2_12: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother, His brothers, and His disciples — and they stayed there a few days.
43_2_13: The Passover of the Jews was near, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
43_2_14: In the temple He found those selling oxen, sheep, and doves, and the money-changers sitting at their tables.
43_2_15: So He made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple — the sheep and the oxen too. He scattered the coins of the money-changers and overturned their tables.
43_2_16: To those selling doves He said, "Get these things out of here! Do not turn My Father's house into a marketplace!"
43_2_17: His disciples remembered that it is written: "Zeal for Your house will consume Me."
43_2_18: The Jewish leaders responded, "What sign can You show us to prove You have the authority to do this?"
43_2_19: Jesus answered them, "Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
43_2_20: The Jewish leaders said, "It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and You will raise it up in three days?"
43_2_21: But He was speaking about the temple of His body.
43_2_22: So when He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this, and they believed the Scripture, and the word that Jesus had spoken.
43_2_23: While He was in Jerusalem during the Passover feast, many believed in His name when they saw the signs He was doing.
43_2_24: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, because He knew them all,
43_2_25: and because He did not need anyone to testify about what was in a person — He Himself knew what was in every person.
43_3_1: There was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
43_3_2: This man came to Jesus by night and said to Him, "Rabbi, we know You are a teacher who has come from God — for no one can do these signs that You do unless God is with him."
43_3_3: Jesus answered him, "Truly, truly, I tell you — unless a person is born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
43_3_4: Nicodemus said to Him, "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter his mother's womb a second time and be born?"
43_3_5: Jesus answered, "Truly, truly, I tell you — unless a person is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
43_3_6: What is born of the flesh is flesh; what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
43_3_7: Do not be amazed that I said to you, 'You must be born from above.'
43_3_8: The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit."
43_3_9: Nicodemus answered, "How can these things be?"
43_3_10: Jesus answered, "You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know these things?
43_3_11: Truly, truly, I tell you — We speak of what We know and bear witness to what We have seen, and yet you do not receive Our testimony.
43_3_12: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
43_3_13: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven — the Son of Man.
43_3_14: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
43_3_15: so that whoever believes in Him may have eternal life."
43_3_16: For God so loved the world that He gave His one-and-only Son, so that everyone who believes in Him will not perish but have eternal life.
43_3_17: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but so that the world might be saved through Him.
43_3_18: The one who believes in Him is not condemned; but the one who does not believe stands already condemned, because he has not believed in the name of the one-and-only Son of God.
43_3_19: And this is the verdict: the Light has come into the world, but people loved the darkness rather than the Light — because their deeds were evil.
43_3_20: Everyone who practices evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light, so that his deeds may not be exposed.
43_3_21: But the one who does what is true comes into the Light, so that his deeds may be clearly seen — that they have been carried out in God.
43_3_22: After these things, Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, and He stayed there with them and was baptizing.
43_3_23: John also was baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there, and people were coming and being baptized —
43_3_24: for John had not yet been thrown into prison.
43_3_25: A dispute arose between some of John's disciples and a Jew over ritual purification.
43_3_26: They came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, the One who was with you on the other side of the Jordan — the One you testified about — look, He is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him!"
43_3_27: John answered, "A person can receive nothing unless it has been given to him from heaven.
43_3_28: You yourselves are my witnesses that I said, 'I am not the Christ — I have been sent ahead of Him.'
43_3_29: The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands by and listens to him, rejoices with great joy at the bridegroom's voice. So this joy of mine is now made full.
43_3_30: He must increase; I must decrease."
43_3_31: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.
43_3_32: He testifies to what He has seen and heard, and yet no one receives His testimony.
43_3_33: Whoever has received His testimony has set his seal to this: that God is true.
43_3_34: For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God — for God gives the Spirit without measure.
43_3_35: The Father loves the Son and has given all things into His hand.
43_3_36: The one who believes in the Son has eternal life, but the one who refuses to believe the Son will not see life — for the wrath of God remains on him.
43_4_1: Now the Lord became aware that the Pharisees had heard He was making and baptizing more disciples than John —
43_4_2: though Jesus Himself was not baptizing; His disciples were —
43_4_3: so He left Judea and went back into Galilee.
43_4_4: And He had to pass through Samaria.
43_4_5: So He came to a Samaritan town called Sychar, near the plot of ground Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
43_4_6: Jacob's well was there. Jesus, worn out from the journey, sat down just as He was, beside the well. It was about the sixth hour.
43_4_7: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Give Me a drink" —
43_4_8: for His disciples had gone off into the town to buy food.
43_4_9: So the Samaritan woman said to Him, "How is it that You, a Jew, are asking me for a drink — a Samaritan woman?" (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
43_4_10: Jesus answered her, "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who is saying to you, 'Give Me a drink,' you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water."
43_4_11: "Sir," she said to Him, "You have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. Where then would You get this living water?
43_4_12: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank from it himself — along with his sons and his livestock?"
43_4_13: Jesus answered her, "Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again.
43_4_14: But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again — ever. The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life."
43_4_15: The woman said to Him, "Sir, give me this water, so I will not be thirsty — and so I will not have to keep coming here to draw."
43_4_16: He told her, "Go, call your husband, and come back here."
43_4_17: The woman answered, "I do not have a husband." Jesus said to her, "You are right in saying, 'I do not have a husband' —
43_4_18: for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband. What you have said is true."
43_4_19: "Sir," the woman said to Him, "I see that You are a prophet.
43_4_20: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where people must worship is in Jerusalem."
43_4_21: Jesus said to her, "Woman, believe Me — an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.
43_4_22: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know — for salvation is from the Jews.
43_4_23: But an hour is coming, and is already here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth — for these are the worshipers the Father is seeking.
43_4_24: God is spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and in truth."
43_4_25: The woman said to Him, "I know that Messiah is coming — the one called 'Christ.' When He comes, He will explain everything to us."
43_4_26: Jesus said to her, "I am He — the One speaking to you."
43_4_27: Just then, His disciples came back. They were amazed that He was speaking with a woman. But none of them asked, "What do You want?" or "Why are You talking with her?"
43_4_28: So the woman left her water jar, went off into the town, and said to the people,
43_4_29: "Come — see a Man who told me everything I have ever done! Could this possibly be the Christ?"
43_4_30: They went out of the town and were coming toward Him.
43_4_31: Meanwhile, the disciples were urging Him, "Rabbi, eat something."
43_4_32: But He told them, "I have food to eat that you do not know about."
43_4_33: So the disciples said to one another, "Could someone have brought Him something to eat?"
43_4_34: Jesus said to them, "My food is to do the will of the One who sent Me, and to finish His work.
43_4_35: Do you not say, 'Four more months, and then the harvest'? Look — I tell you — lift up your eyes and see the fields: they are already white, ready for harvest.
43_4_36: The reaper is already being paid; he is gathering fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
43_4_37: For in this the saying rings true: 'One sows, and another reaps.'
43_4_38: I sent you to reap what you did not labor for. Others have labored, and you have come into the benefit of their labor."
43_4_39: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Him because of the word of the woman who testified, "He told me everything I ever did."
43_4_40: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they urged Him to stay with them — and He stayed there two days.
43_4_41: And many more believed because of His word.
43_4_42: They said to the woman, "It is no longer because of what you said that we believe — now we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this truly is the Savior of the world."
43_4_43: After the two days, He left there for Galilee.
43_4_44: For Jesus Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.
43_4_45: So when He came into Galilee, the Galileans welcomed Him — they had seen everything He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they too had gone to the feast.
43_4_46: He came again to Cana in Galilee, where He had made the water wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
43_4_47: When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, he went to Him and begged Him to come down and heal his son — for he was at the point of death.
43_4_48: So Jesus said to him, "Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe."
43_4_49: The royal official said to Him, "Sir, come down before my little boy dies!"
43_4_50: Jesus said to him, "Go — your son lives." The man believed the word Jesus had spoken to him, and went on his way.
43_4_51: As he was going down, his servants met him and told him that his boy was alive.
43_4_52: So he asked them what hour he began to get better. They told him, "Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him."
43_4_53: Then the father knew that it was at that very hour Jesus had said to him, "Your son lives." And he himself believed — and his whole household.
43_4_54: This was now the second sign Jesus performed, when He had come from Judea into Galilee.
43_5_1: After this, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
43_5_2: Now in Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there is a pool — called Bethesda in Hebrew — which has five covered colonnades.
43_5_3: In these lay a crowd of disabled people — blind, lame, paralyzed — waiting for the water to be stirred.
43_5_4: For at certain times an angel of the Lord went down into the pool and stirred the water. Whoever stepped in first, after the water was stirred, was healed of whatever ailment he had.
43_5_5: And there was a certain man there who had been in his sickness for thirty-eight years.
43_5_6: When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had already been there a long time, He said to him, "Do you want to be healed?"
43_5_7: The sick man answered Him, "Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred. And while I am trying to get there, someone else steps down ahead of me."
43_5_8: Jesus said to him, "Get up. Pick up your mat and walk."
43_5_9: At once the man was made whole — he picked up his mat and began walking. Now that day was a Sabbath.
43_5_10: So the Jewish leaders said to the man who had been healed, "It is the Sabbath. It is not lawful for you to carry your mat."
43_5_11: He answered them, "The one who made me whole — He Himself said to me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
43_5_12: They asked him, "Who is this Man who told you, 'Pick up your mat and walk'?"
43_5_13: But the healed man did not know who it was — Jesus had slipped away, for there was a crowd in the place.
43_5_14: Afterward, Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Look — you have been made whole. Do not sin anymore, so that nothing worse happens to you."
43_5_15: The man went off and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had made him whole.
43_5_16: So the Jewish leaders began to persecute Jesus, because He was doing these things on the Sabbath.
43_5_17: But Jesus answered them, "My Father has been working until now, and I too am working."
43_5_18: This was why the Jewish leaders were all the more trying to kill Him — because He had not only broken the Sabbath, but was also calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.
43_5_19: So Jesus answered them, "Truly, truly, I tell you — the Son can do nothing on His own initiative; He can do only what He sees the Father doing. For whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
43_5_20: For the Father loves the Son and shows Him everything He Himself is doing. And He will show Him greater works than these, so that you will be amazed.
43_5_21: Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whomever He wills.
43_5_22: For the Father judges no one; instead, He has given all judgment into the hands of the Son,
43_5_23: so that everyone may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
43_5_24: Truly, truly, I tell you — the one who hears My word and believes the One who sent Me has eternal life. He does not come into judgment, but has crossed over from death into life.
43_5_25: Truly, truly, I tell you — an hour is coming, and is already here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
43_5_26: For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.
43_5_27: And He has given Him the authority to carry out judgment — because He is the Son of Man.
43_5_28: Do not be amazed at this, for an hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
43_5_29: and will come out — those who have done good into a resurrection of life, and those who have practiced evil into a resurrection of judgment.
43_5_30: I can do nothing on My own initiative. As I hear, I judge — and My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will but the will of the One who sent Me.
43_5_31: If I bear witness about Myself, My testimony does not stand as proof.
43_5_32: There is another who bears witness about Me, and I know that the testimony He bears about Me is true.
43_5_33: You yourselves sent to John, and he has borne witness to the truth.
43_5_34: Not that I rely on human testimony — but I say these things so that you may be saved.
43_5_35: He was the lamp that was burning and shining, and you were willing for a while to rejoice in his light.
43_5_36: But the witness I have is greater than John's. For the very works the Father has given Me to finish — the works I am doing — bear witness about Me, that the Father has sent Me.
43_5_37: And the Father who sent Me — He Himself has borne witness about Me. You have never heard His voice, nor seen His form,
43_5_38: and you do not have His word abiding in you — because you do not believe the One He sent.
43_5_39: You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life. And these very Scriptures bear witness about Me.
43_5_40: Yet you are not willing to come to Me, that you may have life.
43_5_41: I do not receive glory from people.
43_5_42: But I know you — you do not have the love of God within you.
43_5_43: I have come in My Father's name, and you do not receive Me. If another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
43_5_44: How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another, but do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
43_5_45: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. The one who accuses you is Moses — the one in whom you have set your hope.
43_5_46: If you believed Moses, you would believe Me — for he wrote about Me.
43_5_47: But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My words?"
43_6_1: After this, Jesus went off to the other side of the Sea of Galilee — also called the Sea of Tiberias.
43_6_2: A great crowd followed Him, because they had seen the signs He was performing on those who were sick.
43_6_3: Jesus went up on the mountainside and sat down there with His disciples.
43_6_4: The Passover — the feast of the Jews — was near.
43_6_5: So Jesus lifted up His eyes, and seeing that a huge crowd was coming toward Him, He said to Philip, "Where are we to buy bread so that these people may eat?"
43_6_6: He said this to test him, for He Himself knew what He was about to do.
43_6_7: Philip answered Him, "Two hundred denarii's worth of bread would not be enough for each of them to get a little!"
43_6_8: One of His disciples — Andrew, Simon Peter's brother — said to Him,
43_6_9: "There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two small fish. But what is that among so many?"
43_6_10: Jesus said, "Have the people sit down." Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down — about five thousand of them.
43_6_11: Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed them to those sitting down — as much as they wanted — and likewise with the fish.
43_6_12: When they had eaten their fill, He said to His disciples, "Gather up the leftover pieces, so that nothing is wasted."
43_6_13: So they gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves, left over by those who had eaten.
43_6_14: When the people saw the sign Jesus had performed, they began saying, "Truly — this is the Prophet who is to come into the world!"
43_6_15: Then Jesus, knowing that they were about to come and take Him by force to make Him king, withdrew again to the mountain — alone.
43_6_16: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea.
43_6_17: They got into a boat and started across the sea toward Capernaum. By now it was dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
43_6_18: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew rough.
43_6_19: When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walking on the sea, drawing near to the boat — and they were afraid.
43_6_20: But He said to them, "It is I — do not be afraid."
43_6_21: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the land for which they had been heading.
43_6_22: The next day, the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the sea realized that only one small boat had been there, and that Jesus had not gotten into the boat with His disciples — but His disciples had gone away alone.
43_6_23: Other small boats from Tiberias came near the place where they had eaten the bread, after the Lord had given thanks.
43_6_24: So when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there — and neither were His disciples — they got into the boats and came to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
43_6_25: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they said to Him, "Rabbi, when did You get here?"
43_6_26: Jesus answered them, "Truly, truly, I tell you — you are looking for Me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and had your fill.
43_6_27: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures into eternal life — the food which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has set His seal."
43_6_28: So they said to Him, "What must we do to carry out the works of God?"
43_6_29: Jesus answered them, "This is the work of God — that you believe in the One He has sent."
43_6_30: So they said to Him, "Then what sign are You going to do, so we may see it and believe You? What work will You perform?
43_6_31: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness — as it is written, 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
43_6_32: Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you — it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven; My Father is giving you the true bread from heaven.
43_6_33: For the bread of God is the One who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world."
43_6_34: So they said to Him, "Sir, give us this bread always."
43_6_35: Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life. The one who comes to Me will never hunger, and the one who believes in Me will never thirst.
43_6_36: But as I told you, you have seen Me — and still you do not believe.
43_6_37: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never cast out.
43_6_38: For I have come down from heaven — not to do My own will, but the will of the One who sent Me.
43_6_39: And this is the will of the One who sent Me: that I should lose nothing of all He has given Me, but raise it up on the last day.
43_6_40: For this is the will of My Father: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him should have eternal life — and I Myself will raise him up on the last day."
43_6_41: So the Jewish leaders grumbled about Him, because He had said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven."
43_6_42: They said, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, 'I have come down from heaven'?"
43_6_43: Jesus answered them, "Stop grumbling among yourselves.
43_6_44: No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him — and I Myself will raise him up on the last day.
43_6_45: It is written in the Prophets, 'And they will all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard the Father and has learned from Him comes to Me.
43_6_46: Not that anyone has seen the Father — except the One who is from God. He has seen the Father.
43_6_47: Truly, truly, I tell you — the one who believes has eternal life.
43_6_48: I am the bread of life.
43_6_49: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
43_6_50: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
43_6_51: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And the bread I will give for the life of the world is My flesh."
43_6_52: The Jewish leaders then argued with one another, saying, "How can this Man give us His flesh to eat?"
43_6_53: So Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you — unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in yourselves.
43_6_54: The one who feeds on My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
43_6_55: For My flesh is true food, and My blood is true drink.
43_6_56: The one who feeds on My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.
43_6_57: Just as the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father — so the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
43_6_58: This is the bread that came down from heaven — not as the fathers ate and died. The one who feeds on this bread will live forever."
43_6_59: He said these things while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.
43_6_60: When many of His disciples heard this, they said, "This is a hard teaching. Who can listen to it?"
43_6_61: But Jesus, knowing in Himself that His disciples were grumbling about this, said to them, "Does this offend you?
43_6_62: What then — if you should see the Son of Man ascending to where He was before?
43_6_63: It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I have spoken to you — they are spirit, and they are life.
43_6_64: But there are some of you who do not believe." For Jesus knew from the beginning which ones did not believe, and who was going to betray Him.
43_6_65: And He said, "This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless it has been granted to him by the Father."
43_6_66: From that point on, many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
43_6_67: So Jesus said to the twelve, "You do not want to go away also, do you?"
43_6_68: Simon Peter answered Him, "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.
43_6_69: We have come to believe — and we know — that You are the Holy One of God."
43_6_70: Jesus answered them, "Did I not choose you, the twelve? And yet one of you is a devil."
43_6_71: He was speaking of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot — for it was he, though one of the twelve, who was going to betray Him.
43_7_1: After these things, Jesus went about in Galilee. He did not want to go about in Judea, because the Jewish leaders were looking to kill Him.
43_7_2: Now the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was at hand.
43_7_3: So His brothers said to Him, "Leave here and go into Judea, so that Your disciples may see the works You are doing.
43_7_4: For no one does anything in secret who wants to be known in the open. If You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world!"
43_7_5: For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.
43_7_6: Jesus said to them, "My time has not yet come — but for you, the time is always right.
43_7_7: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
43_7_8: You yourselves go up to the feast. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet fully come."
43_7_9: Having said this, He remained in Galilee.
43_7_10: But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, then He Himself also went up — not openly, but as though in secret.
43_7_11: So the Jewish leaders were looking for Him at the feast, and asking, "Where is that Man?"
43_7_12: And there was much muttering about Him among the crowds. Some were saying, "He is a good man." Others were saying, "No — He is leading the people astray."
43_7_13: But no one spoke openly about Him, for fear of the Jewish leaders.
43_7_14: Now about the middle of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and began teaching.
43_7_15: The Jewish leaders were astonished and said, "How does this Man know the Scriptures, when He has never studied?"
43_7_16: Jesus answered them, "My teaching is not My own; it comes from the One who sent Me.
43_7_17: If anyone wants to do His will, he will know about the teaching — whether it is from God, or I am speaking on My own authority.
43_7_18: The one who speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but the One who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him — He is true, and there is no unrighteousness in Him.
43_7_19: Did not Moses give you the law? And yet none of you keeps the law. Why are you trying to kill Me?
43_7_20: The crowd answered, "You have a demon! Who is trying to kill You?"
43_7_21: Jesus answered them, "I did one work, and you all marvel.
43_7_22: Moses gave you circumcision — not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers — and on the Sabbath you circumcise a man.
43_7_23: If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with Me because I made a whole man well on the Sabbath?
43_7_24: Stop judging by outward appearance — judge with right judgment."
43_7_25: Then some from Jerusalem began saying, "Is not this the Man they are trying to kill?
43_7_26: And look — He is speaking openly, and they say nothing to Him! Have the rulers truly come to know that this is the Christ?
43_7_27: But we know where this Man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from."
43_7_28: Then Jesus, teaching in the temple, cried out: "You know Me, and you know where I am from. And yet I have not come on My own — but the One who sent Me is true, and you do not know Him.
43_7_29: I know Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me."
43_7_30: Then they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him — because His hour had not yet come.
43_7_31: Yet many in the crowd believed in Him, and they said, "When the Christ comes, will He do more signs than this Man has done?"
43_7_32: The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these things about Him, and the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to arrest Him.
43_7_33: Then Jesus said, "A little while longer I am with you, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.
43_7_34: You will look for Me and will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come."
43_7_35: So the Jewish leaders said to one another, "Where is He about to go, that we will not find Him? Is He about to go to the dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
43_7_36: What did He mean when He said, 'You will look for Me and will not find Me,' and, 'Where I am, you cannot come'?"
43_7_37: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and cried out, "If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink!
43_7_38: Whoever believes in Me — as the Scripture has said — 'Out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.'"
43_7_39: Now He said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were about to receive. For as yet the Spirit had not been given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
43_7_40: When they heard these words, some of the crowd began saying, "This truly is the Prophet."
43_7_41: Others said, "This is the Christ." But some were saying, "Surely the Christ is not going to come out of Galilee, is He?
43_7_42: Has not the Scripture said that the Christ is to come from the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?
43_7_43: So there was a division in the crowd because of Him.
43_7_44: Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid hands on Him.
43_7_45: The officers then came to the chief priests and Pharisees, who said to them, "Why did you not bring Him?"
43_7_46: The officers answered, "Never has any man spoken like this!"
43_7_47: So the Pharisees answered them, "Have you been led astray too?
43_7_48: Have any of the rulers believed in Him? Or any of the Pharisees?
43_7_49: But this crowd that does not know the law — they are accursed!"
43_7_50: Nicodemus — who had come to Him earlier, and was one of them — said to them,
43_7_51: "Does our law judge a man before it first hears him and knows what he is doing?"
43_7_52: They answered him, "Are you also from Galilee? Search and see — no prophet arises from Galilee."
43_7_53: And everyone went off to his own house.
